Subject: Post-call: token volumes, budget range & EU residency impact

Hi Elena / James —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can size a few realistic options:

- Your goals: embed clinical notes + provide assistant-style summaries to clinicians; GDPR/data residency in the EU is a hard requirement for patient data.
- Estimated monthly usage (your estimate on the call): 20–40M tokens/month across generation + embeddings.
- Token mix you mentioned: roughly 70% embeddings (search/semantic similarity) and 30% generation (summaries/assistant).
- Target unit economics: you said procurement prefers a target in the ballpark of $1k–$1.5k per 1M tokens (we'll unpack generation vs embedding unit costs).

Ask 1 — please confirm the expected steady-state monthly token range (low / expected / high). That will determine whether a hosted or dedicated/private deployment is the right pricing path.
Ask 2 — confirm whether ALL PHI/clinical data must remain in an EU region (yes/no), or whether non-PHI metadata can be processed in the US.

Next steps from our side: I’ve attached a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) and a short EU pricing grid draft. Marissa (SE) and Monica (acct exec) copied — we’ll produce a three-option pricing matrix (hosted EU, dedicated EU reserve, private on-prem estimate) with estimated $/1M token units and any required commit.

Proposed time to review the matrix: Thu or Fri morning next week (your timezone).

Thanks —

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the recap — accurate summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Steady-state estimate: low 18M, expected 28M, high 42M tokens/month. Peaks during nightly batch processing and when large clinician cohorts run retrospective summaries.
- Data residency: yes — any PHI must remain in EU-hosted infrastructure. Non-PHI (hashed user ids, search indices) can be stored/processed outside EU if that simplifies cost, but we'd prefer everything in-region if the delta is reasonable.
- Budget: the procurement team indicated a willingness to evaluate up to ~€1.1k–€1.4k per 1M tokens (generation-equivalent) if SLA and controls are in place. Total monthly budget target (vendor spend) is in the €30k–€45k range initially.

A couple of details that affect unit economics: 1) embeddings are about ~3x cheaper than generation for our expected model mix, and 2) we will use longer context windows for summaries which increases per-request token counts.

We can do Thu 14:00 CEST to review the pricing matrix. Also can you share any example contracts or minimum-commit language for dedicated/private deployments?

Best,

Thanks — quick SE perspective and ballpark economics to set expectations before Thu's review:

- Hosted EU (multi-tenant, regional): typical baseline for a mixed workloads (embeds+gen) — rough blended list: €850–€1,100 per 1M generation-equivalent tokens depending on model family and burst patterns. EU hosting typically adds a 5–12% region uplift vs US hosted due to infra costs and capacity.

- Dedicated EU reserved capacity: unit price drops with commit; for a 20–40M token profile we expect to quote ~€700–€950 /1M with a 3–6 month minimum commit. There is a 20–30% discount band if you commit to a 12-month reserved pool and agree to a predictable request profile.

- Private (VPC / on-prem): pricing is a mix of infra + software fee. For EU-only on-prem that requires a customer-managed cluster, plan for a one-time setup + monthly platform fee; effective unit economics typically need 50M+ tokens to make sense unless you require full air-gap controls. Janitorial items: KMS integration, SOC 2 attestation support, audit log export.

- Important: data residency + private deployment are the main drivers of uplift. If you can tolerate non-PHI in US for caching/indices we can reduce the EU-only footprint and get closer to US list-equivalent prices (roughly 8–12% lower).

Actionable asks for pricing matrix:
1) Priyom — confirm exact expected high/low/opt monthly tokens (Elena provided ranges; pick specific numbers we’ll model on).
2) Monica — please prepare two MAP variants: 3-month pilot (lower commit, higher unit) and 12-month reserved (lower unit, commit).
3) Priyom + Monica — collect procurement questions re: contract minimums and billing cadence.

I’ll draft a simple table showing: model family, region (US/EU), deployment (hosted/dedicated/private), list € /1M, estimated monthly spend at low/expected/high.

—Marissa
